1: The unit vectors i and j separate the two directions, so the magnitude follows from Pythagoras on the components. Writing vectors this way makes addition and subtraction component by component.
2: The constant-acceleration formulae come from integrating acceleration to get velocity and velocity to get displacement. They apply only while the acceleration is constant, so check that before using them.
3: Gradient on a displacement–time graph is velocity, because velocity is the rate of change of displacement. On a velocity–time graph the area under the line is the displacement, which is why the same graph gives both quantities.
